## Historical audit: S0069

**Scope:** Only chunk 3 is visible. All citations below refer to S0069, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. Image paths are recorded, but their pixels are not available to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Student model request, JSONL line 22, chars [0,246526) | The stated goal was an editable reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, matching geometry and viewpoint. The student’s inferred scene was a kitchen showroom. Code defined multiple separate assets: architecture, columns, cabinets, ovens, island, sink, hob, extractor and kettle. Names and inventory do not independently establish reference fidelity. |
| Same event: draft and source-audit exchange | The controller requested checks before execution, not a visual diagnosis. The student added dimension, endpoint and duplicate-key assertions, World initialization, and descendant-mesh traversal with material copies for local extractor bump shading. It modeled wood grain, floor joints, colored finishes and lighting. These are code-level measures, not proof of texture fidelity or material isolation under every edit. |
| Same event: step 1 result and revision | The runner reported `ok: true` and a saved render. The student described the kitchen as too small, the post too central and shell surfaces obstructive; it hypothesized camera distance and azimuth as causes. It moved the camera inside, changed lens and viewpoint, moved/narrowed the foreground post and extended the shell. These are the student’s observations and hypotheses, not independently viewed pixels. |
| Same event: step 2 result and revision | Another successful render was reported. The student reported island and post boundary crossings and a cropped extractor; it hypothesized excessive camera proximity. The next program moved the camera back, repositioned the post, raised the ceiling and extended the extractor with suspension rods. This changed several related parameters together, so their individual effects are unresolved. |
| Same event: step 3 result; lines 23 [0,4403), 24 [0,362), 25 [0,57) | Step 3 also reported `ok: true`, a saved image and blend file. Final review offered selection or `DONE`; the student returned `DONE`, and the controller selected step 3. The final session recorded no tool calls. This establishes successful builds and selection, **not formal reconstruction correctness**. |

**Connections and pose:** Code groups extractor parts and suspension under one asset and assigns island, plinth and fittings positions; this is evidence of intended assembly and placement, not geometric verification of contacts or complete composite movement. No independent pose or occlusion check is visible to this audit. The runner logged 16 samples despite source requesting 48; the trace does not establish why or its visual effect.

**Teacher and exploration:** No teacher message, teacher diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or student adoption of one is visible in this chunk. The source-audit and render-review prompts are controller input. The student made its own successive production revisions within the supplied constraints; diagnostic probes were unavailable. Earlier unseen chunks cannot establish or negate additional input.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Separating reported discrepancies from camera hypotheses and preserving editable groups are transferable practices; the particular kitchen inventory and camera adjustments are task-specific. Whether the final framing, lighting, materials, supports and object inventory match the photograph remains unknown without the images and independent validation. No algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is shown; visual and formal outcome remain unknown.
